text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Manchester City and Brighton.

Manchester City host Brighton at the Etihad Stadium as Pep Guardiola’s side look to avoid a third consecutive Premier League loss, after they suffered back-to-back defeats to Arsenal and Wolves before the international break.
City have won each of their last 20 games in all competitions at home, and they could climb to the top of the table with three points today.
The Sky Blues haven’t lost three Premier League games in a row since 2016, so they will be desperate to steer clear of matching that unwanted statistic here.
Brighton will be hoping to leapfrog a host of teams to get into the Champions League places, but it certainly won’t be easy for Roberto De Zerbi’s side against the champions of England.
The Seagulls haven’t won in four games in all competitions, and they are yet to win away from home against Man City in a league fixture after 13 attempts (D2 L11).

The away side will be hoping to regain some momentum after a poor run of form, and a victory over Guardiola’s team could be the perfect opportunity to boost their confidence after the international break.
Guardiola has opted to make five changes from Man City’s defeat to Arsenal in the Premier League last time out.
Ederson, Ake, Kovacic, Dias, and Lewis all drop to the bench with Stones, Rodri, Akanji, Doku, and Ortega coming in.
Rodri has returned to the starting XI after serving his three-game ban for a sending-off against Nottingham Forest.
Meanwhile, De Zerbi has made three changes from Brighton’s 2-2 draw with Liverpool before the international break.
Steele, Welbeck, and Milner come into the side, with Verbruggen, Ferguson, and Veltman all having to settle for a place on the bench.
The teams are out on the pitch as we edge closer to kick-off!
Welbeck gets the game under way at the Etihad!
Walker gives away an early foul on Mitoma deep inside his own half.
Brighton will now look to pack the box and create an opportunity in the opening few minutes, but it comes to nothing.
Pedro finds Mitoma inside the Man City box with a neat throughball.
However, the Brighton winger struggles to find a team-mate with his cross and the move breaks down.
Early chance for City.
Foden dances through the Brighton midfield, cutting inside onto his favoured left foot.
He finds Doku in space on the edge of the box, but his curling effort goes wide of the post.
GOOOOAALLLL!!! 1-0 CITY!!! Alvarez with the finish! Doku receives the ball out wide and stands up his marker, before dribbling between the Brighton defenders and bursting into the box.
The Belgian winger finds Alvarez in space near the penalty shot, and he scuffs a shot into the roof of the net beyond Steele.
It's the ideal start for Guardiola's side!
Doku evaded multiple challenges on the left-hand side, dancing through the Brighton defence, before laying the ball on a platter for Alvarez.
Doku is causing major problems on the City left so far.
Once again, he darts beyond Milner and gets to the byline, but his cross is comfortably dealt with by Dunk and the danger is cleared.
Silva does well to link up with Gvardiol deep inside the Brighton half.
The Croatian finds himself in space on the edge of the box and has a go from range with his weak foot, but it's easily saved by Steele.
Welbeck is struggling with an injury and the play has stopped so he can receive treatment.
It could be an early blow for De Zerbi if the Brighton forward has to be substituted.
Brighton are forced into an early change as Welbeck is unable to continue.
Ferguson enters the fray.
GOOOAAAALLLL!!! 2-0 CITY!! Haaland with a superb finish! Guardiola's side pressed high and pounced on Baleba in midfield with Silva winning possession in a dangerous position.
The ball fell to Haaland, who charged towards the Brighton penalty area and unleashed a thunderous strike from outside of the box.
It's a nightmare start for De Zerbi and his team, they have a mountain to climb now!
Doku again makes things happen in the final third.
He receives the ball out wide and Milner starts to back off.
The City winger finds a yard of space and drills the ball into the Brighton box, but it evades every attacker and the Seagulls can clear the danger.
City have enjoyed more of the ball in the early proceedings, having 52.9 per cent of the possession with Brighton struggling to deal with Guardiola's attack.
VAR is checking an incident involving Alvarez off the ball.
After a short delay, the game resumes with no action taken.
The Seagulls are struggling to get out of their half as City continue to pressure De Zerbi's defence at every opportunity.
The Brighton manager won't be happy with his team's performance so far.
Foden looks to find the run of Haaland in behind the Brighton defence, but Igor is equal to it and glances a header out for a corner.
The Norwegian striker was lurking and it's an important interception from the defender.
City don't appear to be satisfied with just the two goals so far today!
Doku once again evades multiple challenges from the Brighton defence, cutting inside and looking to cause problems in the final third.
He darts towards the penalty area and tries to find Alvarez with a throughball, but Dunk deals with the situation well and clears.
Brighton have tested Ortega in the City goal just once so far this game with one shot on target.
Guardiola's side have managed three so far, with two of them finding the back of the net.
March is the first player to go into the referee's book for a poor challenge in the middle of the pitch.
He can have no complaints.
City once again look to test Brighton's defence as Doku finds Silva in the box with a smart throughball.
The Portuguese midfielder dinks it over the goalkeeper but after a scramble in the penalty area, the ball is cleared.
Rodri picks up a booking for kicking the ball away after Doku was flagged for offside.
Doku bursts into the box, using his pace to leave Milner for dead before getting to the byline once again.
He cuts it back, looking to find a City attacker, but Dunk slides in and clears the ball away.
Guardiola's side have remained on top throughout the first half and are pushing to get a third.
Brighton continue to try and play out from the back despite City pressing high and regularly winning the ball in the final third.
They're going to need to improve drastically in the second half to avoid conceding more goals.
The fourth official has indicated that there will be a minimum of four minutes of added time in the first half.
The pace of the game has started to slow down as City appear to be content with going into the break with a 2-0 lead.
Guardiola's side are keeping possession and staying patient, with Brighton sitting back and absorbing the pressure.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 BRIGHTON
City go into the break with a 2-0 lead over Brighton.
Guardiola's side opened the scoring early in the first half, with Alvarez finding himself in space in the box after some excellent work down the left from Doku.
The Argentine dispatched the ball beyond Steele with an unorthodox finish.
The Seagulls struggled to get going and their day got worse after Welbeck suffered an injury shortly after the first goal.
The Sky Blues doubled their lead later in the half as Haaland pounced on a mistake in the middle of the pitch and found the back of the net from just outside the box.
De Zerbi won't be happy with his team's performance in the opening 45 minutes and they will need to see a vast improvement to be able to get something from this game.
City have looked back to their best after two consecutive Premier League defeats before today.
Doku has been the standout player so far, and it was a difficult half for Milner, who has the task of dealing with the tricky winger.
A reaction is needed from Brighton, and Guardiola will be hoping to see a carbon copy of the first half when the players return to the pitch.
Brighton make their second change of the game as Veltman comes on for Milner at the break.
The second half is under way at the Etihad!
Brighton are enjoying more of the ball in the opening few minutes of the second half.
De Zerbi's side need to show more of an attacking threat to get back into this game.
Doku goes down under the challenge of Veltman and looks in some discomfort.
Thankfully, the City winger doesn't need treatment and he looks as though he will be able to carry on.
CHANCE! Adingra finds Gross inside the City box in space with a superb throughball between the defenders.
The Brighton midfielder evades the offside trap and closes in on Ortega, but he gets his shot all wrong and it goes wide of the post.
He should have done better!
Foden uses his pace to skip past March on the right-hand side and finds himself inside the Brighton box.
His cross deflects off the defender and almost creeps behind for a corner, but Steele collects and the Seagulls regain possession.
March had to be careful not to bring the England international down after his early booking in the first half.
It's been a second half of few opportunities for both teams.
Neither side have managed more than one touch in the opposition box since the game got back under way.
Igor makes a reckless challenge on Stones on the edge of his own box and City are awarded a free-kick.
Alvarez and Silva are standing over it as Steele sets up his wall.
Alvarez looks to curl it towards the top corner, but it flies over the bar.
Foden and Doku link up well deep inside the Brighton half as the former latches onto a throughball in the penalty area.
He fires a cross into the danger zone, but Steele gets a hand to it and diverts it away from the City attackers waiting in the middle.
Mitoma darts through the middle of the pitch before Akanji brings him down with a professional foul, picking up City’s second booking of the game.
Igor is the latest player to go into the book after a late challenge on Rodri, who had poked the ball past the Brighton defender.
Pedro's afternoon is over as De Zerbi rolls the dice, bringing on Fati at the Etihad.
Gilmour replaces Baleba in the Brighton midfield as they make their fourth change of the game.
CHANCE! City could be three goals to the good.
Foden finds Haaland beyond the Brighton defence with a perfectly weighted pass.
The prolific striker controls the ball well and cuts back onto his left foot, before looking to bend one beyond Steele.
However, the keeper makes an excellent save to keep the game at 2-0.
It's now Brighton's turn to test the opposition's resolve.
Mitoma finds himself in space behind the defensive line after an impressive throughball by Fati.
The Japan winger looks to dink the ball over Ortega who rushes out to close the angle, but he gets it all wrong and the City stopper makes the save.
Doku looks to get on the scoresheet as he sprints towards the Brighton defence at pace, but his shot is tame and Steele makes a comfortable save.
De Zerbi will be impressed with how Brighton have managed to deal with the City winger in the second half.
GOOOALLLL!!!! Brighton are back in it! 2-1!!! The Seagulls pull one back.
Mitoma twists and turns as he approaches the City box and manages to evade the challenge of Walker.
His cross only finds Akanji but the defender fails to clear it and Fati is there to place the ball beyond Ortega in goal.
Game on!
Dias enters the fray in place of Stones in the City defence.
Doku leaves the pitch in place of Grealish in a straight swap on the left-hand side of attack.
Brighton have enjoyed more of the ball in the second half with 57.8 per cent of the possession, as they look to get a result against City after a disappointing opening 45 minutes.
City are pushing to grab a third goal now and put the game out of sight, but they're struggling to find a breakthrough as De Zerbi's side remain resolute at the back.
The fans at the Etihad wait nervously with the Seagulls now back in the match.
Gvardiol picks up the ball inside his own half and looks to burst through the Brighton midfield.
The Croatian evades multiple challenges and closes in on the edge of the box, but Dunk is equal to it and the danger is cleared.
Grealish is the latest player to go into the referee's book for protesting against a decision from one of the officials.
Haaland uses his pace and strength to carry the ball from his own half and win a free-kick to settle the game down.
Gilmour and Veltman both attempted to dispossess the Norwegian and failed, with his determination to keep possession too much for the Brighton duo to handle.
March is down and looks in a lot of pain after a hefty challenge and he's now receiving treatment.
Brighton appear to be readying another substitution as it looks as though he won't be able to carry on.
There will be four minutes of added time at the end of the second half at the Etihad.
The game is yet to restart with it looking like a potentially serious injury for March, who is now being carried off on a stretcher.
The Etihad gives him a standing ovation.
Van Hecke comes on in place of March after his injury late in the second half.
RED CARD! Akanji gets his marching orders! The City defender is sent off after receiving a second yellow card for pulling down Fati on the counter.
Guardiola makes a change to try and see out the game after the red card, with Ake coming on in place of Alvarez.
Brighton are pushing for an equaliser! Gross bursts into the box and looks to drill the ball into the middle, but it's blocked and out for a corner in the dying minutes.
De Zerbi's side are in the ascendency with City down to 10 men.
Brighton's corner comes to nothing, and that may just be that at the Etihad!
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-1 BRIGHTON
City hold on and secure a 2-1 victory over Brighton at the Etihad.
It was looking like a comfortable game for Guardiola's side after goals from Alvarez and Haaland saw them go into the break with a 2-0 lead over the Seagulls.
The second half started slowly with De Zerbi's men pushing to get back into the game, before Fati pulled one back to force an exciting end to the match.

City remained resolute at the back before Akanji was sent off, but even when depleted, they absorbed the late pressure and came away with three points! City will be looking to carry their momentum into the Champions League next week against Young Boys, while Brighton will be hoping to bounce back against Ajax in the Europa League on Thursday.
That's all for today, goodbye!
